<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Epístola ad Romános
<r>Rom 13:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Omnis ánima potestátibus sublimióribus súbdita sit: non est enim potéstas nisi a Deo: quæ autem sunt, a Deo ordinátæ sunt.
<n>2</n> Itaque qui resístit potestáti, Dei ordinatióni resístit. Qui autem resístunt, ipsi sibi damnatiónem acquírunt:
<n>3</n> Nam príncipes non sunt timóri boni óperis, sed mali. Vis autem non timére potestátem? Bonum fac: et habébis laudem ex illa;
<n>4</n> Dei enim miníster est tibi in bonum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Illumináre, illumináre Ierúsalem, quia venit lux tua:
* Et glória Dómini super te orta est.
<r>℣.</r> Et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, et reges in splendóre ortus tui.
<r>℟.</r> Et glória Dómini super te orta est.
b.a068417852:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May God the Father Omnipotent, be to us merciful and clement.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans
<r>Rom 13:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Let every soul be subject to higher powers: for there is no power but from God: and those that are, are ordained of God.
<n>2</n> Therefore he that resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God. And they that resist, purchase to themselves damnation.
<n>3</n> For princes are not a terror to the good work, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? Do that which is good: and thou shalt have praise from the same.
<n>4</n> For he is God's minister to thee, for good. But if thou do that which is evil, fear: for he beareth not the sword in vain.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Shine, shine, O Jerusalem, for thy light is come;
* And the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
<r>℣.</r> And the Gentiles shall walk in thy light, and kings in the brightness of thy rising.
<r>℟.</r> And the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Rom 13:4-7</r>
<n>4</n> Si autem malum féceris, time: non enim sine causa gládium portat. Dei enim miníster est: vindex in iram ei, qui malum agit.
<n>5</n> Ideo necessitáte súbditi estóte non solum propter iram, sed étiam propter consciéntiam.
<n>6</n> Ideo enim et tribúta præstátis: minístri enim Dei sunt, in hoc ipsum serviéntes.
<n>7</n> Réddite ómnibus débita: cui tribútum, tribútum: cui vectígal, vectígal: cui timórem, timórem: cui honórem, honórem.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Omnes de Saba vénient, aurum et thus deferéntes, et laudem Dómino annuntiántes,
* Allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Reges Tharsis et ínsulæ múnera ófferent, reges Arabum et Saba dona addúcent.
<r>℟.</r> Allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
b.55b702d7f1:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May Christ to all His people give, for ever in His sight to live.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Rom 13:4-7</r>
<n>4</n> For he is God's minister: an avenger to execute wrath upon him that doth evil.
<n>5</n> Wherefore be subject of necessity, not only for wrath, but also for conscience' sake.
<n>6</n> For therefore also you pay tribute. For they are the ministers of God, serving unto this purpose.
<n>7</n> Render therefore to all men their dues. Tribute, to whom tribute is due: custom, to whom custom: fear, to whom fear: honour, to whom honour.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> All they from Saba shall come, they shall bring gold and incense, and they shall show forth the praises of the Lord.
* Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents, the kings of Arabia and Saba shall offer gifts.
<r>℟.</r> Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>Rom 13:8-10</r>
<n>8</n> Némini quidquam debeátis, nisi ut ínvicem diligátis: qui enim díligit próximum, legem implévit.
<n>9</n> Nam, Non adulterábis, Non occídes, Non furáberis, Non falsum testimónium dices, Non concupísces: et si quod est áliud mandátum, in hoc verbo instaurátur: Díliges próximum tuum sicut teípsum.
<n>10</n> Diléctio próximi malum non operátur. Plenitúdo ergo legis est diléctio.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Magi véniunt ab Oriénte Ierosólymam, quæréntes, et dicéntes: Ubi est qui natus est, cuius stellam vídimus?
* Et vénimus adoráre Dóminum.
<r>℣.</r> Vídimus stellam eius in Oriénte.
<r>℟.</r> Et vénimus adoráre Dóminum.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Et vénimus adoráre Dóminum.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>Rom 13:8-10</r>
<n>8</n> Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For he that loveth his neighbour hath fulfilled the law.
<n>9</n> For: Thou shalt not commit adultery: Thou shalt not kill: Thou shalt not steal: Thou shalt not bear false witness: Thou shalt not covet. And if there be any other commandment, it is comprised in this word: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
<n>10</n> The love of our neighbour worketh no evil. Love therefore is the fulfilling of the law.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> There came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, asking and saying: Where is He That is born King of the Jews? for we have seen His star in the east;
* And are come to worship the Lord.

<r>℟.</r> And are come to worship the Lord.

b.fa97d0c6b3:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uinto Idus Ianuárii Luna prima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ, sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno, natális sanctórum Iuliáni Mártyris, et Basilíssæ Vírginis, ipsíus Iuliáni uxóris. Hæc, virginitáte cum viro suo serváta, in pace vitam finívit; Iuliánus vero (postquam multitúdo Sacerdótum et Ministrórum Ecclésiæ Christi, quæ, propter immanitátem persecutiónis, ad eos confúgerat, igne cremáta est), Marciáni Prǽsidis iussu, plúrimis torméntis cruciátus, capitálem senténtiam accépit. Cum ipso étiam Antónius Présbyter, et Anastásius, quem idem Iuliánus, a morte suscitátum, grátiæ Christi partícipem fécerat, et Celsus puer cum huius matre Marcionílla, ac septem fratres, aliíque plúrimi passi sunt.
<h>S</h>myrnæ sanctórum Mártyrum Vitális, Revocáti et Fortunáti.
<h>I</h>n Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Epictéti, Iucúndi, Secúndi, Vitális, Felícis et aliórum septem.
<h>I</h>n Mauritánia Cæsariénsi sanctæ Marciánæ Vírginis, quæ, béstiis trádita, martýrium consummávit.
<h>S</h>ebáste, in Arménia, sancti Petri Epíscopi, fílii sanctórum Basilíi et Emméliæ, atque fratris item sanctórum Basilíi Magni et Gregórii Nysséni Episcopórum, ac Macrinæ Vírginis.
<h>A</h>nconæ sancti Marcellíni Epíscopi, qui urbem illam (ut sanctus Gregórius Papa scribit) divína virtúte ab incéndio liberávit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.41d44df97c:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>anuary 9th 2027, the 1st day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Antioch, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the holy martyr Julian, along with whom is commemorated the holy Virgin Basilissa, his wife, who kept her virginity with her husband and ended her life in peace. A multitude of priests and ministers of the Church of Christ had taken refuge with them because of the fury of the persecution. They were burnt with fire, and Julian, by command of the President Marcian, was thereafter made to suffer many torments and was then beheaded.
<h>A</h>long with him there suffered also the Priest Anthony and Anastasius, whom Julian had raised from the dead and made a partaker of the grace of Christ, and the lad Celsus, together with his mother, Marcionilla, and seven brethren, and many others.
<h>A</h>t Smyrna, the holy martyrs Vitalis (probably a Bishop, and the others were most likely Deacons), Revocatus, and Fortunatus.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Epictetus, Jucundus, Secundus, Vitalis, Felix, and seven others, (in the year 205.)
<h>I</h>n Morocco, (in the fourth century,) the holy Virgin and martyr Marciana, who was thrown to wild beasts and so finished her testimony.
<h>A</h>t Sebaste, in Armenia, (in the year 392,) holy Peter, Bishop (of that see,) brother of holy Basil the Great (also of St. Gregory of Nyssa. His father was St. Basil the Elder, his mother St. Emmelia, and his grandmother St. Macrina. He was made head of his convent in the year 362, when St. Basil was made bishop, St. Basil having before been Abbot thereof.)
<h>A</h>t Ancona, holy Marcellinus, Bishop of that city, the which, as holy Gregory writeth, he did through the power of God deliver from burning. (He succeeded St. Traso in the Bishopric about the year 550, and was followed by St. Thomas about the year 569. He is secondary Patron of Ancona.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
